items.title: Milt Fillius interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 18, 2000
items.q: I look at guys like Haggart and Ralph Sutton and guys like that who were drunks when they were young.

ctx.x: Yes. And it’s so curious. I mean we have done 190 to date. And when I think back on it, the unpleasant experiences I’ve had with these musicians, are on one hand. And that is really saying something.

Well the people we’ve dealt with have a talent. They’ve all got a God-given talent, and that makes them different. I look at guys like Haggart and Ralph Sutton and guys like that who were drunks when they were young. They more than drank their share. But the guys who made it got smart and got off that stuff, and are the ones who have lasted, the ones that we’re dealing with have all wised up from that. They’ve had that experience. And they make wonderful friends, they really do. And I’m very attached to a lot of…
Well I could argue about that.
